     version instantly once verified. Enables immediate rollback if issues
     arise. Higher infrastructure cost but minimal downtime and fastest
     recovery.
  2. Canary
     Route a small percentage of traffic to the new version while most users
     stay on the old one. Gradually increase traffic if no issues detected.
     Catches problems early with limited blast radius. Slower rollout but safe
     for critical systems.
  3. Rolling
     Update instances incrementally, one at a time or in small batches. Old and
     new versions coexist briefly. Tight resource constraints but lower cost.
     Requires careful backward compatibility and monitoring during the
     transition window.
  4. Immediate (Big-bang)
     Deploy the new version to all instances simultaneously. Fastest possible
     rollout with minimal complexity. High risk if issues are discovered
     post-deployment. Best for non-critical systems or when thorough testing
     eliminates risk.
  5. Type something.
